titulo_es: The passive voice in all tenses
descripcion_es: The passive in continuous and perfect tenses, with modals and infinitives; the passive with get.
resumen: The passive is formed with be in the appropriate tense + past participle. Every tense and every modal has its passive; get + past participle is an informal alternative for changes or events.

filas: The winners will be announced on Monday.
The bridge will have been finished by May.
The letter should have been sent yesterday.

explicacion.texto: Tip: first write the active sentence in its tense, replace the main verb with be in that same tense and add the past participle. Only the form of be changes.
The infinitive and the gerund also have a passive: to be done (I want to be told) and being done (She hates being interrupted).

Get + past participle: more informal, for changes, accidents or something that happens to the subject: He got fired. Our car got stolen. They got married. It is not used with state verbs (not “The house got owned”).

items: By + agent only if it adds information: The novel was written by a teenager.
With two objects, the person is usually made the subject: I was given a prize.
Intransitive verbs (happen, arrive, die) have no passive.

ejemplos.frase: A new hospital is being built near the motorway.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se está construyendo un nuevo hospital cerca de la autopista.

ejemplos.frase: The paintings had been stolen before the alarm went off.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los cuadros habían sido robados antes de que sonara la alarma.

ejemplos.frase: Applications must be submitted before 30 June.
ejemplos.traduccion: Las solicitudes deben presentarse antes del 30 de junio.

ejemplos.frase: The mistake should have been noticed earlier.
ejemplos.traduccion: El error debería haberse detectado antes.

ejemplos.frase: My bike got stolen while I was in the library.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me robaron la bici mientras estaba en la biblioteca.
A nadie le gusta que le mientan.

ejemplos.frase: All the staff were given a bonus last year.
ejemplos.traduccion: A toda la plantilla se le dio una paga extra el año pasado.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The bridge is being built now.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The continuous passive needs being + past participle; the Spanish “pasiva refleja” (with “se”) is not translated with an active verb.
Happen is intransitive: it has no passive.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The report must be finish today.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The report must be finished today.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After modal + be you need the past participle, not the infinitive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the appropriate tense.
ejercicios.frase: Sorry, you can't use this room. It ___ (clean) at the moment.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Present continuous” row of the table applies: am/is/are being + past participle. The clue is at the moment, which indicates an action in progress now, and the subject it (the room), which does not clean but is cleaned. That is why it is is being cleaned. The contraction 's being cleaned is also fine, just as correct in spoken English.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Action in progress now: present continuous passive.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo siento, no puedes usar esta sala. La están limpiando en este momento.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active: it would say that the room is cleaning something. Being + past participle is missing.
It is the present simple passive (habitual); at the moment requires the continuous form is being cleaned.
Been is the past participle of be and does not go after is; the continuous form takes being.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the appropriate tense.
ejercicios.frase: Three new species ___ (discover) in the area since 2020.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Present perfect” row of the table applies: has/have been + past participle. The clue is since 2020, which measures a period up to now and requires the present perfect. The subject three new species is plural, so have, and the species are discovered, hence been discovered.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Since indicates the present perfect: have been + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Desde 2020 se han descubierto tres especies nuevas en la zona.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Since requires the present perfect, not the past simple.
Species is plural here (three new species): have.
It is active: it would say that the species discovered something. Been is missing.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the appropriate tense.
ejercicios.frase: When we arrived, the food ___ (already / eat).
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Past perfect” row of the table applies: had been + past participle. The clue is when we arrived, a past moment, and already, which signals that the action had finished before then. The food is eaten by others, so it is passive. Already goes after had: had already been eaten. The past participle of eat is irregular: eaten.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Something earlier than a past moment: had been + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cuando llegamos, ya se habían comido la comida.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Already goes right after the first auxiliary: had already been eaten.
When we arrived the action had already finished: you need the past perfect, had been eaten.
Ate is the past simple; the past participle is eaten.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive of the modal.
ejercicios.frase: These medicines ___ (should / keep) away from children.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Modal” row of the table applies: modal + be + past participle. The clue is should, a modal, and the subject these medicines, which do not keep anything but are kept. Should is followed by be in the infinitive without to, and then the irregular past participle of keep, kept.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estos medicamentos deben guardarse fuera del alcance de los niños.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active: it would say that the medicines should keep something. Be is missing.
After be comes the past participle, kept.
Should is followed by the infinitive without to.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive of the perfect modal.
ejercicios.frase: The patient ___ (could / save) if the ambulance had come sooner.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Perfect modal” row of the table applies: modal + have been + past participle. The clue is the unreal past condition if the ambulance had come sooner, which requires a perfect modal (something that could have happened and did not). The patient is saved, so it is passive: could have been saved.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Unrealised past possibility in the passive: could have been + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: El paciente se habría podido salvar si la ambulancia hubiera llegado antes.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It refers to the present or future; for an unrealised past possibility you need could have been saved.
It is active: it would say that the patient could have saved someone. Been is missing.
After a modal comes have in the infinitive, never has.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card's rule on the passive gerund applies: being + past participle (She hates being interrupted). The clue is hate, a verb that takes the -ing form, and the passive meaning: I am not the one telling, but the one being told. That is why being told. In English I hate to be told would also exist, but it is not among the options.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Hate takes -ing, and the meaning is passive: being told.
ejercicios.traduccion: Odio que me digan lo que tengo que hacer.

por_opcion.being told: Correct: passive gerund after hate; I receive the action of telling.
por_opcion.be told: Incorrect: hate cannot be followed by an infinitive without to; you would need to be told.
por_opcion.telling: Incorrect: it is active and would mean that I hate telling someone what to do, and even then the object would be missing.
por_opcion.to tell: Incorrect: it is active; it would mean “I hate telling” and the sentence would be incomplete without saying whom.

ejercicios.frase: By next spring, the new stadium ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Future perfect” row of the table applies: will have been + past participle. The clue is by next spring, which sets a future deadline by which the action will already be finished. The stadium is finished by others, so it goes in the passive: will have been completed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Para la próxima primavera, el nuevo estadio estará terminado.

por_opcion.will have been completed: Correct: future perfect passive, an action completed before the deadline.
por_opcion.will have completed: Incorrect: it is active and would say that the stadium will have completed something.
por_opcion.will be completing: Incorrect: it is active and continuous; it would say that the stadium will be completing something at that moment.

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the most natural option in an informal register.
ejercicios.frase: Be careful with that knife or you'll ___ hurt.
ejercicios.explicacion: The get + past participle rule applies: an informal alternative for accidents or changes that happen to the subject (He got fired). The clue is the informal register and the idea of an accident with the knife. Get hurt is a very fixed combination in spoken English, equivalent to Spanish “hacerse daño”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Get + past participle for accidents or changes in informal language.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ten cuidado con ese cuchillo o te vas a hacer daño.

por_opcion.get: Correct: get + past participle, natural for an accident in an informal register.
por_opcion.be being: Incorrect: will be being hurt is a forced form that is hardly ever used and does not express the one-off accident.
por_opcion.have: Incorrect: you'll have hurt would be an active future perfect with no object and makes no sense here.

ejercicios.frase: The new airport is building by a Chinese company.
respuestas: The new airport is being built by a Chinese company.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Present continuous” row of the table and the card's first typical error apply: the continuous passive needs being + past participle. The clue is by a Chinese company, which shows that the airport is being built by someone. Is building is active and would say that the airport is building; you have to say is being built (irregular past participle of build).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Continuous passive: is being + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Una empresa china está construyendo el nuevo aeropuerto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The new airport is building by a Chinese company.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: the continuous passive takes being + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The new airport is being build by a Chinese company.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After being comes the past participle, built.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The new airport is built by a Chinese company.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is passive, but present simple; for work in progress you need is being built.

ejercicios.frase: The accident was happened on the motorway.
respuestas: The accident happened on the motorway.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's rule applies: intransitive verbs (happen, arrive, die) have no passive. The clue is happen, which takes no direct object, so there is nothing that could become the subject of a passive. The active past simple is enough: happened. The calque comes from Spanish “fue ocurrido” or from thinking that “ocurrir” needs to be passive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Happen is intransitive and has no passive.
ejercicios.traduccion: El accidente ocurrió en la autopista.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The accident was happened on the motorway.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: happen is intransitive and has no passive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The accident was happen on the motorway.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is still an impossible passive with an intransitive verb; happened is enough.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The accident has happened on the motorway.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active, but it refers to a specific past event; what is natural and what is required is happened.

ejercicios.frase: The contract will be sign tomorrow.
respuestas: The contract will be signed tomorrow.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Future / will” row of the table and the card's typical error apply: be is always followed by the past participle. The clue is will be, which is already correct, and tomorrow, which confirms the future. Only sign, in the infinitive, is wrong; the regular past participle is signed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Be is always followed by the past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The contract will be sign tomorrow.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: after be comes the past participle signed.
Removing be makes it active, and it would say that the contract will sign something.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The contract will be signing tomorrow.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active continuous; the passive needs the past participle signed.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive without mentioning the agent.
ejercicios.frase: They were interviewing the candidates all morning.
respuestas: The candidates were being interviewed all morning.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Past continuous” row of the table applies: was/were being + past participle. The clue is were interviewing, an active past continuous, and all morning, which stresses the duration. The object the candidates becomes a plural subject, so were being interviewed. They adds no information and is left out.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past continuous passive: were being + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estuvieron entrevistando a los candidatos toda la mañana.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The candidates were interviewed all morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is the past simple passive; the continuous aspect of the original sentence is lost.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The candidates were being interviewing all morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After being comes the past participle, interviewed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The candidates was being interviewed all morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Candidates is plural: were.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive without mentioning the agent.
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Present perfect” row of the table applies: has/have been + past participle. The clue is has stolen, which is in the present perfect, and someone, an unknown agent that is left out. My wallet is singular, so has been, and the past participle of steal is stolen.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle; someone is not mentioned.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Correct as a sentence, but it changes the tense: the active was in the present perfect and the passive must keep it.
It is active: it would say that the wallet has stolen something. Been is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My wallet has been stolen by someone.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The instruction asks you not to mention the agent.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive starting with the person.
ejercicios.frase: The company offered her a promotion.
respuestas: She was offered a promotion by the company.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's rule for verbs with two objects applies: the person is usually made the subject (I was given a prize). The clue is offer, which takes an indirect object (her) and a direct object (a promotion), and the instruction, which asks you to start with the person. Her becomes the subject in the nominative case, she, followed by was offered and the direct object. The agent by the company is optional.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With two objects the person is usually made the subject.

errores_previstos.explicacion: As the subject you must use the subject pronoun she, not her.
After was comes the past participle offered.
It is active and would say that she offered a promotion; was is missing.

respuestas: the mayor should have been invited
should the mayor have been invited
ejercicios.explicacion: The “Perfect modal” row of the table applies: modal + have been + past participle, typical of criticism about the past. The clue is that the words include should, have, been and invited: the mayor is invited. The order is subject + should + have + been + past participle. A question is also possible, with should before the subject.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Passive perfect modal: should have been + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: the mayor should been have invited
errores_previstos.explicacion: The order of the auxiliaries is fixed: modal + have + been + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: the mayor have should been invited
errores_previstos.explicacion: The modal always comes first in the verb phrase.

ejercicios.explicacion: The “Present continuous” row of the table applies: is being + past participle. The clue is that the words include is, being and the past participle watched, and the subject the house, which is being watched. The order is subject + is + being + past participle; in a question, is goes before the subject.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Being goes after is, not before.
Calque of Spanish “está siendo vigilada la casa”: in an affirmative sentence the subject goes first.

descripcion_larga_es: This card extends the passive voice to all tenses and to modals: is being built, has been published, will have been finished, should have been sent. It also covers the passive infinitive and gerund and the informal alternative with get. It is essential for the English of reports, news and procedures, and Spanish speakers find the continuous passive and choosing the right tense of be particularly difficult.

contexto.que_es: It is the passive voice applied to any tense, to modals and to non-finite forms. The rule is always the same: be is conjugated in the tense of the active sentence and the past participle is added. Get + past participle is an informal variant for events or changes that happen to the subject.
contexto.por_que_importa: In the press, reports, minutes and administrative texts the passive appears in all tenses, and a B2 exam requires you to handle it fluently. Getting the form of be wrong changes the tense of the action or produces ungrammatical sentences such as “The bridge is building”. In addition, knowing when to use get helps you sound natural in conversation.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When the action or its result matters more than the agent: work in progress (is being repaired), results (have been published), deadlines (will have been completed), obligations (must be signed) or criticism (should have been noticed). Spanish tends to use the “pasiva refleja” with “se” or the third person plural, and Spanish speakers tend to translate these with an active verb without a real subject.
